set_aside.subject: admission execution policy
set_aside.text: Admission is one recorded verdict over the whole active corpus
set_aside.question: When a trial case can produce different results across executions, how many times is each case executed for admission, and how are differing results combined into the recorded verdict?
options: Execute every active case exactly once and admit if those executions pass
Repeat cases and admit only under a specified stability or aggregation rule
Treat any observed failure during a specified number of executions as refusal
set_aside.default_guess: Execute each active case once and record one aggregate verdict for that admission.

witness.initial: A contract has one trial case expecting value A; its implementation obtains chance through an undetected mechanism and alternates between A and B.
events: An authoring agent submits the implementation.
The kernel performs admission over the active corpus.
outcomes: A kernel executing the case once happens to receive A, records admitted, and activates the implementation.
A kernel repeating the case observes B on a later execution, records refused, and does not activate the implementation.
witness.observer: The submitting agent and anyone who later runs the slot see whether it was activated.

set_aside.subject: identity and reuse of a recorded admission verdict
set_aside.text: Admission is one recorded verdict over the whole active corpus
set_aside.question: If the same immutable implementation is submitted again while the active corpus is unchanged, must the kernel return the existing recorded verdict or execute admission again and record a new verdict; if new verdicts are allowed, which verdict governs admission and rollback eligibility?
options: One verdict is retained per implementation and corpus state and reused on equal resubmission
Every submission performs admission again and the latest verdict governs
Every submission records another verdict, and any admitted verdict over the current corpus remains sufficient
set_aside.default_guess: Retain and reuse one immutable verdict keyed by implementation and the exact active corpus.

witness.initial: An implementation with undetected chance has already been refused over the current corpus after producing a failing output; neither its code nor the corpus has changed.
events: The authoring agent submits byte-for-byte identical code for the same contract version again.
On a fresh execution the implementation would produce the expected output.
outcomes: The kernel returns the existing refused verdict, so the implementation remains inactive.
The kernel reruns admission, records an admitted verdict, and activates the implementation.
witness.observer: The authoring agent sees the verdict, and subsequent flow runners see whether the slot has a current activation.
